mainTopic: Do we follow the רוב (majority) in money cases? The גמרא tests the view that we do, using the case of a slave sold with a hidden flaw and the case of an ox that gored a pregnant cow.
overview: This amud continues the debate between רב and שמואל over whether we follow the רוב (majority) in money cases. First the גמרא tries to prove רב's view from the case of a slave who turns out to be a thief or a gambler, but it rejects the proof because all slaves are assumed to be like that. Next it challenges רב from a משנה about an ox that gored a pregnant cow. The answer is that the רוב shows the ox's attack caused the miscarriage, but we still don't know whether it was fright or goring, so the money is split. The גמרא then tries to match רב and שמואל to a dispute between תנאים about an animal found dead beside a dangerous animal. Both רב and שמואל escape that link by showing that a רוב and a חזקה are not the same. Finally the גמרא challenges רב from the משנה about flaxseed that did not sprout. It answers that רב follows other תנאים, and it begins quoting a ברייתא whose last opinion, from רבי יוסי, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does the slave buyer have no claim?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the sale of a slave who turns out to be a thief or a gambler still stands. It suggests the reason is that most slaves are like that, which would mean we follow the רוב in money matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Isn't it because most slaves are like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the case quoted just before this, where someone sells a slave who turns out to be a thief or a gambler and the sale still stands. It asks why, and suggests the answer is that most slaves are like this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sale stands only because most slaves have these flaws, then the buyer is assumed to know about them because of the majority. That would prove we follow the רוב even in ממון cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not...? (opens a suggested answer)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does the slave sale still stand, even though the slave turned out to be a thief or a gambler?

phrases.english: Is it not because most of them are like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the slave case quoted just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The view that we follow the רוב in ממון matters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a slave sold who turns out to be a thief or a gambler, where the sale stands.

steps.title: No proof, because all slaves are like that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The sale stands because every slave has these flaws, not just most of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, all of them are like this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the slave case. It says every slave is like this, so the case has nothing to do with following a majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all slaves have these flaws, the buyer certainly knew what he was getting, and no majority rule is needed. So the slave case cannot teach us anything about רוב in ממון.

phrases.english: No, all of them are like this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the slave case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed only most slaves are flawed. In fact all are, so the case does not rely on a majority at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The slave case proves nothing about רוב, because every slave is assumed to have these flaws.

steps.title: The case of the ox that gored a pregnant cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. An ox gored a cow, and the cow's calf was found dead beside her. Nobody knows whether the calf was born before or after the goring, and the ox's owner pays half damages for the cow and a quarter for the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An ox gored a cow, and her calf was found beside her. It is not known whether she gave birth before it gored her or after it gored her. The owner pays half damages for the cow and a quarter for the calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a משנה about an ox that gored a pregnant cow. This step sets up a challenge, and the actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שור תם (an ox not known to gore) pays only חצי נזק, half the damage. For the calf the owner pays only a quarter, half of that half, because we are unsure whether the goring caused the calf's death. The money is split down the middle because of the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought)
Half damages (paid for an ox not known to gore)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An ox that gored a cow,
and her fetus was found beside her,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יָדוּעַ אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נְגָחָהּ יָלְדָה,
phrases.english: and it is not known whether she gave birth before it gored her,
or whether she gave birth after it gored her –
he pays half damages for the cow,
and a quarter for the offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שׁוֹר שֶׁנָּגַח אֶת הַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the slave proof was pushed away, the גמרא opens a new line with a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that we follow the רוב in ממון matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the case. The attack itself comes in step 4.

steps.title: Why not follow the majority of cows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner pays only a quarter for the calf. Most cows carry and give birth to live calves, so we should assume the goring caused this miscarriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us say: follow the majority of cows. Most cows become pregnant and give birth normally, so this cow certainly miscarried because of the goring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from the previous step. If we followed the רוב, we would assume the goring killed the calf, and the owner would pay the full half damages for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most cows carry to term and give birth to live calves. So a dead calf beside a gored cow should be blamed on the goring. Since the משנה splits the payment instead, it seems we do not follow the רוב in ממון cases.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the ox is guilty of goring the cow, which is certain. The doubt is only about the calf: was it already born and dead before the goring, or did the goring kill it?

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: Why does the owner pay only a quarter for the calf?

phrases.english: Let us say: follow the majority of cows,
and most cows become pregnant and give birth;
and this one certainly miscarried because of the goring!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא: הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב פָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of the משנה in step 3 to attack the view that we follow the רוב in money matters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that we follow the רוב in ממון matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If we followed the majority, we would assume the goring killed the calf and require the full half damages for it. The משנה requires only a quarter, so it seems the majority is not followed in money cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether we follow the רוב in ממון matters decides many money cases where the facts are unclear, so this question shapes the whole debate.

steps.title: The quarter payment comes from doubt about how the calf died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the cow case says nothing against following the רוב. Even granting that the ox's attack caused the miscarriage, we still do not know whether the goring itself or plain fright caused it. That doubt is a case of ממון המוטל בספק, so the two sides split the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that we are unsure. Maybe the ox came at the cow from the front, and she miscarried from fright. Maybe it came from behind and gored her, and that made her miscarry. So this is money in doubt, and all money in doubt is split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 4. The quarter payment does not come from ignoring the majority. It comes from a different doubt that the majority cannot solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רוב of cows giving birth to live calves tells us this calf was not born normally before the ox came, so the ox's attack led to the miscarriage. It does not tell us how. If the ox came from the front, fright may have caused it, and the owner would not owe for that. If it came from behind, the goring caused it. That doubt is not settled, so the rule of splitting doubtful money applies.

keyTerms.meaning: We are in doubt / we are unsure
Money whose ownership is in doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying we ignore the רוב here. The רוב is accepted. It shows the ox's attack led to the miscarriage, but it cannot tell us whether the cause was fright or the goring itself, and only goring makes the owner pay.

phrases.english: There, it is because we are uncertain,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the ox that gored the pregnant cow, from step 3.

phrases.english: for it is possible to say: it came at her from the front,
and she miscarried from fright;
and it is possible to say: it came at her from behind,
and it actually gored her, and she miscarried;
so it is money that lies in doubt,
and all money that lies in doubt is divided.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4. The רוב shows the miscarriage came from the ox's attack, but the doubt that remains is whether fright or goring caused it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the source of doubt: the majority settles one question, but a second, unsettled question explains the split payment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The quarter payment looked like a refusal to follow the majority of cows that give birth to live calves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The majority is accepted. The split comes from the separate doubt of fright versus goring, which falls under the rule of ממון המוטל בספק.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים about an animal found dead next to a dangerous animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the רב–שמואל dispute may be an older dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא. The תנא קמא says we do not assume a known gorer or biter killed the ox found beside it. רבי אחא says that if a wild camel is found next to a dead camel, we assume it killed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute between תנאים. An ox was grazing, and another ox was found dead next to it. The dead one was gored and the live one is known to gore, or the dead one was bitten and the live one is known to bite. Even so, we do not say for sure that this one gored it or bit it. רבי אחא says: if a wild camel is rampaging among camels and a camel is found dead next to it, we assume this one killed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a ברייתא that it wants to compare to the dispute between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions face the same kind of case. An animal is found dead, and the animal next to it is the type that does such things. The תנא קמא will not blame the dangerous animal without proof. רבי אחא assumes the wild animal did it, because that is how it normally acts.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים
An animal with a proven record of causing a certain damage
It is known / we may assume for certain
Rampaging, acting wild (a male camel in mating season)

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute between Tannaim:
An ox that was grazing,
and an ox was found killed at its side;
even though this one has been gored
and that one is known to gore,
or this one has been bitten and that one is known to bite;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁזֶּה נְגָחוֹ וְזֶה נְשָׁכוֹ.
phrases.english: we do not say: it is certain that this one gored it, or that one bit it.
Rabbi Acha says:
A camel that is rampaging among the camels,
and a camel is found killed at its side —
it is certain that this one killed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line: after defending רב, the גמרא tries to trace the רב–שמואל dispute back to תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא will not assume that a dangerous animal caused a death found next to it. רבי אחא does assume it.

steps.title: Linking רב to רבי אחא and שמואל to the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא thought that רוב and חזקה work the same way. Based on that, it suggests רב (who follows the majority) holds like רבי אחא, and שמואל (who does not) holds like the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that a majority and a presumption are the same thing. So let us say רב, who said we follow the majority, holds like רבי אחא. And שמואל, who said we don't, holds like the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the ברייתא would match רב and שמואל. The whole idea rests on one assumption: that רוב and חזקה are the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחא decides the case from how such an animal usually behaves. That is a חזקה. If a חזקה is just like a רוב, then following one means following the other. So רבי אחא would match רב, and the תנא קמא would match שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed (the people who made this suggestion)
A presumption based on normal behavior
They are the same as each other

phrases.aramaic: סַבְרוּהָ דְּרוּבָּא וַחֲזָקָה כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ;
phrases.english: They assumed that a majority and a presumption are equal;
so let us say that Rav, who said his view, holds like Rabbi Acha,
phrases.notes: רב's view is that we follow the majority in money cases. שמואל's view is that we don't.

phrases.english: and Shmuel, who said his view, holds like the first Tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ דְּרוּבָּא וַחֲזָקָה כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the comparison that step 6 set up.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב–שמואל dispute about following רוב in money cases is the same as the dispute between רבי אחא and the תנא קמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the ox found dead and the rampaging camel, read on the assumption that רוב equals חזקה.

steps.title: רב: the first תנא rejects a חזקה but would still follow a רוב
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the comparison. He can hold his view even according to the תנא קמא. The תנא קמא only refused to follow a חזקה, but he agrees that we follow a רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: I hold my view even according to the first תנא. The first תנא only said, there, that we don't follow a presumption. But a majority, we do follow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the comparison from step 7. It attacks the assumption that רוב and חזקה are the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב separates the two ideas. A רוב is stronger than a חזקה. So even the תנא קמא, who would not blame the dangerous animal based on a חזקה, could agree that we follow a רוב in money cases. That means רב does not need to side with רבי אחא.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (a way of defending someone's view)
He only said his view up to here (and no further)

steps.whatToRemember: רוב and חזקה are not the same. Someone can refuse to rely on a חזקה in money cases and still follow a רוב, so the dispute between רב and שמואל does not have to match the dispute between רבי אחא and the תנא קמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: Telling a majority apart from a presumption is a basic tool that comes up all over the תלמוד whenever we decide facts we cannot see.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
I said my view even according to the first Tanna;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא הָתָם –
phrases.english: the first Tanna only said his view there
because we do not follow a presumption,
but a majority, we do follow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison in step 7 by denying that רוב and חזקה are the same.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link between רב and רבי אחא. It does not decide the dispute between the תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that רוב and חזקה are the same is wrong. A רוב can be followed even by someone who does not follow a חזקה.

steps.title: שמואל can agree even with רבי אחא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says his view fits even רבי אחא, because רבי אחא only followed a חזקה, not a רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל can tell you: My ruling works even according to רבי אחא. רבי אחא only ruled the way he did there because we follow a חזקה, since that animal itself is known to be dangerous. But we do not follow a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as רב pushed away the link to the תנא קמא in step 8, שמואל now pushes away the link to רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 assumed רוב and חזקה work the same way. שמואל says they do not: a חזקה about this very animal is stronger than a general majority. So רבי אחא can follow the חזקה and still agree with שמואל that we do not follow the רוב in money cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling in that case (and not in others)
Known / established, based on how it has behaved before

steps.whatToRemember: Neither רב nor שמואל must be tied to the תנאים in the camel ברייתא. A חזקה about the thing itself is different from a general רוב.

phrases.english: And Shmuel can say to you:
What I said holds even according to Rabbi Acha;

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא הָתָם –
phrases.english: Rabbi Acha only said his ruling there
because we follow a presumption,
since it itself is known to be dangerous;
phrases.notes: He means the presumption comes from this very camel's own wild behavior, not from what most camels do.

phrases.english: but the majority, we do not follow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 8: step 8 freed רב from the link, and this step frees שמואל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the second half of the step 7 suggestion, that שמואל must hold like the תנא קמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 7 treated חזקה and רוב as the same. But a חזקה about the animal itself is stronger, so רבי אחא can follow it without following a רוב.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about seeds that did not sprout
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a seller of produce is not responsible if the buyer planted it and it did not grow, even with flaxseed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone sells produce to his friend, and the friend plants it and it does not sprout, then even if it was flaxseed, the seller is not responsible for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test רב's view. This step quotes the source, and the next step explains why it is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is produce that could be bought either for eating or for planting. The seller does not have to pay back when it fails to grow. The key word to watch is "even" (אפילו), which the גמרא will look at in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source used as a proof or challenge)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who sells produce to his fellow,
and he planted them and they did not sprout;
and even if it was flaxseed —
he is not responsible for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The camel discussion is finished; the גמרא opens a new challenge to רב from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that we follow the רוב in money cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the source is quoted here, and the attack is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: The word "even" shows we don't follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: "Even flaxseed" means: even though most flaxseed is bought for planting, we still don't follow the majority. That goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "even" mean? Doesn't it mean: even flaxseed, which most people buy for planting, and still we do not follow the majority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה is a problem for רב: the word "even" points to a case where the majority clearly favors the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most flaxseed is bought for planting, so if we followed the רוב, we would assume this buyer wanted to plant and the sale was a mistake. Yet the משנה says the seller does not pay. That means the משנה does not follow the רוב, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: What does "even" add? (asking why the word is there)

phrases.english: What does "even" come to teach?
Is it not: even flaxseed,
which most people buy for planting,
and even so
we do not follow the majority?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the challenge from the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that we follow the רוב in money cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "even" shows the משנה is talking about a case where the majority favors the buyer, and still the seller does not pay. So the משנה does not follow the רוב.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב follows other תנאים, and quotes a ברייתא that makes the seller responsible for garden seeds but not for flaxseed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone sells produce to his friend, and the friend plants it and it does not sprout: if it was garden seeds that people do not eat, the seller is responsible. If it was flaxseed, he is not responsible. רבי יוסי says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the משנה goes against רב, but says other תנאים agree with him. It begins quoting a ברייתא to show the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garden seeds are never eaten, so they were surely bought for planting, and the seller must pay. Flaxseed is sometimes eaten, so the first opinion here does not make the seller pay. The opinion of רבי יוסי starts here and continues on the next amud, where we will see who supports רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished yet. רבי יוסי's opinion continues on the next amud, so don't decide who agrees with רב until you see it.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between Tannaim,
as it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר פֵּירוֹת לַחֲבֵרוֹ וּזְרָעָן וְלֹא צִמֵּחוּ;
phrases.english: One who sells produce to his fellow, and he planted them and they did not sprout;
garden seeds, which are not eaten —
he is responsible for them,
flaxseed — he is not responsible for them.
Rabbi Yosei says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 10 and 11 by saying רב has support from other תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge from the משנה, but shows that רב's view is one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה goes against רב, so his view seems to have no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only one opinion. A ברייתא shows another תנא who can support רב (his words follow next).
